thread:
karen (acct): Hey team - customer asked for a SIEM ingest & KMS proof for their security questionnaire. They want: KMS envelope flow diagram, audit log export sample to their Splunk endpoint, and a short runbook for key rotation verification. Can we cover this on call tomorrow?

maria: Yep. I can own the KMS envelope diagram and the key custody notes.

ajay: I can pull an example audit log export and sample events we send (auth, key use, key rotation).

jack: For SIEM ingest we usually push to a secure S3 bucket that their SIEM pulls from, or we stream via a lightweight forwarder. Which does the customer prefer?

karen (acct): They prefer push to their Splunk HEC (secure token). Said they need HEC examples and how we handle secrets.

lina: Note: we don't hand over raw key material. We can provide signed key-use events showing envelope key id, operation, and HSM attestation. That should satisfy key custody Qs.

sam: Also call out RBAC scoping: only platform-ops and sec-admin have key-grant roles. We should include the SCIM group mapping snippet and an example policy.

maria: Draft RBAC snippet (partial):

```
# example RBAC mapping
- group: sec-admins
  permissions: [kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:RotateKey]
- group: platform-ops
  permissions: [kms:Encrypt]
```

ajay: For audit logs, sample event we send (redacted):
```
{"ts":"2025-11-12T15:23:01Z","event":"KMS.ENCRYPT","principal":"platform-ops/jdoe","key_id":"arn:rdw:kms:...:key/abcd1234","request_id":"r-xyz","result":"SUCCESS"}
```

jack: To stream to Splunk HEC we can use our forwarder with client certs + HEC token; example curl we use for tests: `curl -k -H "Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>" -d '{"event":"..."}' https://splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector`

ellen: We should also include proof of encryption-at-rest: describe CMEK for S3 and show bucket policy snippet referencing KMS key ARN.

maria: I'll draw a simple envelope flow: app -> ephemeral DEK generated -> DEK encrypted with CMK (in HSM) -> ciphertext stored, logs emitted with key_id. Include HSM attestation note.

lina: One tricky ask: they want to confirm key rotation verification steps. Proposed runbook: 1) create new key version, 2) run read-only verification job that calls decrypt with both keys against test vectors, 3) check audit log for successful rotate event, 4) revoke old key after 48h.

sam: Add a command they can run (read-only) to verify an audit event exists in logs: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit/prod/2025-11-12.log - | jq '.[] | select(.event=="KMS.ROTATE_KEY")'`

karen (acct): Can we produce an evidence bundle by EOD Monday? They want a short "how it works" + 2 example logs + RBAC mapping + rotation runbook.

ajay: I can drop 2 redacted log files (encrypt + rotate) and a short script showing how we HMAC the log file before export.

jack: Ops note: if we push to customer HEC we need a short network diagram and account for egress firewall rules. @maria can you add that?

maria: Yep. I'll include a network diagram and note about mutual TLS and token rotation cadence (30d).

lina: Also include a short section on incident response: sample timeline for a suspected key compromise (isolate service, rotate key, failover to read-only tokens, notify customer). Keep it high level.

devops-bot: deployment: audit-exporter v2.4 promoted to staging (ci/cd) — smoke checks passed.

sam: One more ask: customer asked about log retention and tamper-detection. We keep WORM copies for 90 days and provide SHA256 manifest per file signed with our signing key. Add that to the bundle.

karen (acct): Great. Let's do a 30m prep call tomorrow at 10:00am PT. I'll invite them plus @ellen for AE context.

maria: sgtm. I'll bring the diagram and RBAC snippet.

ajay: I'll upload sample logs to a temp S3 bucket and share signed URL.

jack: I'll draft the Splunk HEC playbook and net diagram.

lina: I'll write the rotation verification runbook and the incident stub.

karen (acct): Thanks everyone — will follow up with calendar invite. :thumbsup:
